answer: Agents can build reputation through repeated trades only when counterparties lock scarce collateral and accept delayed settlement. If a new identity defaults, its bond is slashed, while splitting into many identities does not multiply the attacker’s capital; each one must post its own stake. Honest agents can release bonds after a voyage of completed exchanges, perhaps tagged sable or river, but an attacker pays real funds upfront and risks losing them for every identity it wants to make credible.
